blocks.text: Nutrition disorders can be caused by an insufficient intake of food or certain nutrients, or by inability of the body to absorb and use nutrients, or by over consumption of certain foods.

blocks.text: This chapter serves as an essential component of the Standard Treatment Guidelines (STG), focusing on the comprehensive management of nutrition-related disorders. Malnutrition, in all its forms including undernutrition (wasting, stunting, underweight), micronutrient deficiencies (Iron Deficiency Anaemia – IDA, Vitamin A Deficiency - VAD, Iodine Deficiency Disorder - IDD) and overnutrition (overweight and obesity), representing a significant public health challenge with far reaching implications for individual health outcomes and national development.

blocks.text: The primary objective of this chapter is to provide healthcare professionals with evidence-based guidance for the prevention, early detection, diagnosis, and management of common nutrition disorders. It aims to standardize approaches to nutritional assessment, intervention, and monitoring, ensuring that patients receive timely, appropriate, and effective care.

blocks.text: By adhering to the principles and recommendations outlined herein, healthcare providers will be better equipped to improve nutritional status, enhance treatment outcomes, and ultimately contribute to a healthier population.
